title: MS NOW Wants to Turn Its Viewers Into a Fandom
gist: MS NOW (formerly MSNBC) president Rebecca Kutler describes launching 'MS NOW Membership,' a talent-centric paid subscription built after surveying 18,000 people, designed to convert a large digital/YouTube audience (90% of whom don't watch linear TV) into paying members, while framing the network's post-NBCUniversal spinoff into Versant as a capital-allocation unlock and downplaying near-term risk from cable's secular decline.

themes.theme: Membership launch: applying the influencer playbook to news

insights.claim: MS NOW is launching a paid subscription program called 'MS NOW Membership' centered on giving members direct, scheduled access to its on-air talent rather than just gating articles or video behind a paywall.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: A legacy cable news brand is explicitly adopting a creator/influencer monetization model (direct fan access to named personalities) instead of a standard commodity-news paywall — a template other struggling media brands with strong on-air talent could copy.
insights.locator: she's launching an ambitious subscription program

insights.claim: Before designing the Membership offering, MS NOW surveyed and interviewed roughly 18,000 people over about a year and a half of product research rather than building what Kutler called 'another commodity news app.'
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: Heavy upfront primary research (18k respondents) is an unusually rigorous product-development process for a media subscription launch, suggesting management conviction in the offer's fit before committing to it.
insights.quote: We went out to 18,000 people. We did surveys, we did in-person interviews, and we spent time taking that research and getting to where we are this week.
insights.locator: When we started this process around a year and a half ago

insights.claim: The Membership product includes twice-daily (noon and 6pm, seven days a week) live interactive sessions where paying members can directly question a rotating slate of named MS NOW anchors and contributors, including Rachel Maddow, Michael Steele, Jen Psaki, and Al Sharpton.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: A high-frequency, talent-access cadence (14 sessions/week) is the concrete mechanism intended to justify the subscription price and drive retention — a metric worth tracking (session attendance, churn) once disclosed.
insights.quote: Seven days a week at noon and at 6:00 pm, if you are a member of the MS NOW community, you can hop on and directly interact with one of our anchors or one of our reporters.
insights.locator: It's taking our current superfans who watch us on linear

insights.claim: Kutler explicitly frames the Membership launch as unfinished by design, stating the product will look 'vastly different' in six months to a year as the team iterates based on usage data rather than trying to get everything right at launch.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: An explicit iterate-in-public product philosophy signals management expects (and is prepared for) early feature/pricing changes — useful context for judging early reviews or complaints about the launch version.
insights.quote: what you see this week will look vastly different six months from now and a year from now if we're doing our jobs right.
insights.locator: What I most want people to know

insights.claim: MS NOW says it is currently the second most-watched basic cable news channel behind Fox News.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: Self-reported cable ranking (unverified against Nielsen in the article) frames MS NOW's negotiating position for affiliate fees and ad rates relative to its main cable rival.
insights.quote: We're actually right now the number two most-watched basic cable channel.
insights.locator: We have a huge cable audience

insights.claim: MS NOW claims its digital properties draw more unique visitors than Axios, Politico, and The Atlantic, and more time spent per visitor than the Washington Post and NPR, and that it generates more YouTube clicks than ABC News, NBC News, and CBS News combined.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: If accurate, these are strong digital-scale claims for a network still branded mainly as a cable channel — a potential re-rating case for how investors value MS NOW/Versant's digital audience versus cable-only comparables. Self-reported metrics, no independent source cited, so treat as management claim not verified fact.
insights.quote: People spend more time with us digitally than places like the Washington Post and NPR.
insights.locator: But that's just one piece of our business

insights.claim: Roughly 90 percent of the people who consume MS NOW on YouTube, digital, social, or audio do not regularly watch the network's linear cable television programming.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: A 90% non-overlap between digital and linear audiences means the Membership subscription is targeting an almost entirely separate, previously unmonetized funnel rather than cannibalizing existing cable subscribers — a materially larger total addressable market than cable-only figures suggest.
insights.quote: All those people consuming us on YouTube, on digital, on social, in audio, 90 percent of those people do not regularly consume us on linear television.
insights.locator: Is the goal to pull linear viewers onto digital

insights.claim: MS NOW's average cable viewer watches about nine hours of programming per week, which Kutler cites as evidence the core cable business is 'quite healthy' in the near term even as she acknowledges the audience skews older and faces long-term secular decline.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: A bullish near-term/cautious long-term framing from a cable news executive is a useful anchor for modeling the pace of cable-news ad and affiliate revenue erosion versus a cliff scenario.
insights.quote: Our average viewer watches nine hours a week.
insights.locator: I am not blind to the long-term challenges

insights.claim: MS NOW (formerly MSNBC) was spun out of NBCUniversal roughly a year ago into a new standalone company called Versant, which also holds CNBC, E!, and golf-related media assets.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: Establishes the corporate structure investors need to evaluate MS NOW under: no longer a line item inside a theme-park-and-studios conglomerate, but part of a smaller, cash-generative cable-and-digital-focused portfolio (Versant).
insights.quote: Versant is the spinoff, so a spinout, of NBCUniversal. For folks that weren't following along day by day, around a year ago, NBCUniversal spun out a series of businesses.
insights.locator: What is Versant, for those who may not know?

insights.claim: Under prior NBCUniversal ownership, MS NOW's investment was constrained because the parent had to allocate capital across a much broader portfolio including theme parks; under Versant, cash the network generates is reinvested back into MS NOW specifically.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: A direct causal claim that spinning a cable news asset out of a diversified conglomerate increases capital available for reinvestment in that asset — a thesis worth testing against other media conglomerate breakups (e.g., Warner Bros. Discovery's split).
insights.quote: We are now part of a company that is incentivized to invest the money that we earn as MS NOW back into MS NOW.
insights.locator: When you're working for the very large, very successful companies

insights.claim: Kutler characterizes NBCUniversal's prior underinvestment in MS NOW/MSNBC as a rational portfolio-allocation decision for that parent company rather than a failure specific to the network.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: A non-adversarial framing of the prior parent suggests management is not looking to publicly relitigate the spinoff, useful context for reading Versant/NBCUniversal relations going forward.
insights.quote: So what they did makes sense for them.
insights.locator: I think that because of the life that this brand lived

themes.theme: Competitive stance versus Fox and industry consolidation

insights.claim: Kutler says MS NOW is competing across every platform simultaneously — cable, digital, YouTube, and audio — rather than defining its competitive set narrowly as the cable news landscape against Fox.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: Signals management is benchmarking success on cross-platform reach metrics, not just Nielsen cable ratings — relevant to how analysts should evaluate the network going forward.
insights.quote: I just see who our competition is as wider than that typical cable landscape.I want to build a great product right now and have a large membership community, and I want to make sure that we are competing on every battleground.
insights.locator: Are you competitive? Do you want to beat Fox?

insights.claim: MS NOW positions its audience as progressive/Democratic-leaning under a self-described 'pro-democracy' banner, explicitly distinct from and minimally overlapping with Fox News's Republican-leaning audience.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: Confirms MS NOW is not chasing audience-neutrality but doubling down on a partisan-aligned niche — relevant to modeling its addressable subscriber ceiling versus a broader-appeal strategy.
insights.quote: Is the audience for MS NOW different from the audience for Fox? Of course it is. There's probably a small amount of overlap, but not a lot, and that's OK.
insights.locator: I would say MS NOW reaches progressives

insights.claim: Asked about a possible merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery that would combine CNN and CBS News under one owner, Kutler said she is 'rooting for' stronger, healthier newsrooms industry-wide, including a stronger CNN, despite CNN being a competitor.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: A competitor executive's publicly cooperative (non-adversarial) stance toward a potential rival-strengthening merger is a signal that incumbent news executives may not fight industry consolidation, easing a path for such deals to close without vocal industry opposition.
insights.quote: In a functioning healthy democracy, you need a very healthy free and fair press. So I am rooting for better, stronger newsrooms.
insights.locator: I'm curious about your take on the possibility of a merger

insights.claim: MS NOW deliberately avoids pushing every on-air host onto every social platform, instead matching individual talent to the platforms where they are organically strong — for example Symone Sanders Townsend on TikTok/Instagram versus Lawrence O'Donnell's strength on YouTube.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: A reusable talent-deployment framework for any media brand monetizing personality-driven content: match creator to native platform rather than forcing uniform omnichannel presence, which likely improves ROI per platform investment.
insights.quote: One of my rules is: don’t do anything that feels weird for you. What I mean by that is, if you in your own life don’t use TikTok, I don’t recommend trying to become a TikToker.
insights.locator: What has the experience been like of transitioning

insights.claim: Kutler states a belief that content quality is the decisive competitive factor for media brands trying to break through digital noise, over platform-native gimmicks or algorithm-chasing tactics.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: A stated executive priority (content depth over algorithmic optimization) that investors can use to judge whether MS NOW's resource allocation (staffing, production spend) matches its stated strategy.
insights.quote: I might be old-school when I say this, but I think content always wins. Every single race.
insights.locator: I think that's the answer to the question of how do you break through
